output: {"objective":"Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of BTK-p.Arg28His (BTK, UniProt Q06187) and test it with one targeted computational test.","subject":{"gene":"BTK","variant_id":"BTK-p.Arg28His","accession":"Q06187","position":28,"reference_residue":"R","alternate_residue":"H","protein_change":"p.Arg28His"},"events":52,"current_favourite":"H1","hypotheses":[{"id":"H1","mechanism_class":"ligand_binding","starting_rank":1,"statement":"[Agent-generated hypothesis] Arg28 sits in the BTK PH-domain inositol-phosphate pocket, and His28 cannot make the same charge-based contacts with the 4-, 3- and 1-phosphates of IP4 or PIP3, so the PH domain loses membrane-anchoring affinity and BTK fails to be recruited to the plasma membrane.","supports":["E2","E3","E5","E6","E16","E13"],"would_refute":"Ligand-bound experimental structures (for example 1B55 with 4IP) show Arg28 side-chain atoms more than about 4.5 Å from every inositol phosphate phosphate oxygen, and a modelled R28H complex (same ligand, His28 rotamers sampled) keeps the same contact count and buried-surface area as Arg28 within noise.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H2","mechanism_class":"protein_interaction","starting_rank":2,"statement":"[Agent-generated hypothesis] His28 disrupts the PH-TH module homodimer interface that stabilises the active, membrane-bound BTK conformation, so R28H loses the dimer-driven increase in kinase activity without changing the PH-domain fold.","supports":["E7","E11","E9"],"would_refute":"In the modelled or experimental PH-TH dimer (for example from the 2025 dimerisation study's structure), Arg28 has no atom within about 5 Å of the second protomer, and an R28H homodimer model keeps the same inter-protomer contact area and interface energy as wild type.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H3","mechanism_class":"stability_folding","starting_rank":3,"statement":"[Agent-generated hypothesis] The His side chain at position 28 perturbs local PH-domain packing or backbone dynamics near the N-terminal beta-strands, lowering the folded fraction and thermal stability so that less BTK is correctly folded at the membrane.","supports":["E13","E14","E15","E17","E8"],"would_refute":"Predicted stability change (for example FoldX or Rosetta ddG on the 6TT2 or 1B55 backbone) for R28H is below about 1 kcal/mol, and the R28H model shows no change in per-residue RMSF or contact-order around residues 20-40 compared with wild type over short molecular dynamics runs.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"}],"results":[{"test_id":"T1","test_kind":"ligand_contact","summary":"Residue 28 lies within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 ligand-bound structures that observe it, with closest approach 2.58 Å to 4PT in PDB 2Z0P (chain C 2.58 Å, chain A 2.59 Å) and 2.58 Å to A1B6K in 7I9B. Contacting ligands include 4IP (4 of 6 instances, min 2.75 Å), 4PT (4 of 4, min 2.58 Å), and several A1B6x tetrahydrobenzofuran ligands (min 2.58–3.13 Å). Negative-control ligands (3IS, 72V, A1JS1, IS7, MG, NYQ, Q1B, ZN) never contacted the residue, and the four R28C-mutated structures (6TT2, 6TSE, 1BTK, 6YYF) showed 0 contacting ligand instances.","headline":"Residue 28 is within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 ligand-bound structures (4IP, 4PT, A1B6F, A1B6G, A1B6H, A1B6I); closest 2.58 Å to 4PT ((2R)-3-{[(S)-{[(2S,3R,5S,6S)-2,6-DIHYDROXY-3,4,5-TRIS(PHOSPHONOOXY)CY…) in PDB 2Z0P.","verdict":"contact_with_organic_ligand","job_id":null}]}
